nānvaye'pi bhayaṃ tasya jāya te sarpasaṃbhavam .. 43 ..
5.182.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते स्नानं सकृद्भक्त्या समन्वितः ..
नान्वयेऽपि भयं तस्य जाय ते सर्पसंभवम् .. 43 ..
5.182.m:
Whoever performs ritual ablution there once, endowed with devotion,
no fear arising from snakes occurs even in his family lineage.

5.182.s:
tatra yacchati miṣṭānnaṃ dvijānāṃ sajjanaiḥ saha ..
pūjayitvā tu nāgeṃdrānsanātanapuraḥsarān .. 44 ..
5.182.d:
तत्र यच्छति मिष्टान्नं द्विजानां सज्जनैः सह ..
पूजयित्वा तु नागेंद्रान्सनातनपुरःसरान् .. 44 ..
5.182.m:
Whoever offers sweet food to brahmins there along with good people,
having worshipped the serpent lords headed by Sanātana,

5.182.s:
saptajanmāṃtaraṃ yāvanna sa dauḥsthyamavāpnuyāt ..
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ śākinīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
na cchidraṃ na ca rogāśca nādhayo na riporbhayam .. 45 ..
5.182.d:
सप्तजन्मांतरं यावन्न स दौःस्थ्यमवाप्नुयात् ..
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां शाकिनीनां विशेषतः ..
न च्छिद्रं न च रोगाश्च नाधयो न रिपोर्भयम् .. 45 ..

5.182.s:
yaścaitacchṛṇuyādbhaktyā vācyamānaṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
so'pi saṃvatsaraṃ yāvatpannagairna ca pīḍyate .. 46 ..
5.182.d:
यश्चैतच्छृणुयाद्भक्त्या वाच्यमानं द्विजोत्तमाः ..
सोऽपि संवत्सरं यावत्पन्नगैर्न च पीड्यते .. 46 ..
5.182.m:
And whoever hears this recited with devotion, O best of brahmins,
he too will not be afflicted by serpents for a whole year.

5.182.s:
sarpadaṣṭasya yasyaitatpurataḥ paṭhyate bhṛśam ..
nāgatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ kāla daṣṭo'pi jīvati .. 47 ..
5.182.d:
सर्पदष्टस्य यस्यैतत्पुरतः पठ्यते भृशम् ..
नागतीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं काल दष्टोऽपि जीवति .. 47 ..
5.182.m:
Before one who is bitten by a snake, if this māhātmya
of Nāgatīrtha is continuously recited, he lives even if bitten by Time [itself].

5.182.s:
pustake likhitaṃ caitannāgatīrthasamudbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ tiṣṭhate yatra na sarpastatra tiṣṭhati .. 48 ..
5.182.d:
पुस्तके लिखितं चैतन्नागतीर्थसमुद्भवम् ..
माहात्म्यं तिष्ठते यत्र न सर्पस्तत्र तिष्ठति .. 48 ..
5.182.m:
And wherever this māhātmya originating from Nāgatīrtha
remains written in a book, no snake stays there.

5.182.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye nāgatīrthotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma tryaśītyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 183 ..
5.182.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये नागतीर्थोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्र्यशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 183 ..
5.182.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-third chapter, entitled “Description of the Origin and Māhātmya of Nāgatīrtha,” in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.183.s:
.. .. sūta uvāca .. ..
tṛtīye ca dine prāpte trayodaśyāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
prātaḥsavanamādāya ṛtvijaḥ sarva eva te ..
svesve karmaṇi saṃlagnā yajñakṛtyasamudbhave .. 1 ..
5.183.d:
.. .. सूत उवाच .. ..
तृतीये च दिने प्राप्ते त्रयोदश्यां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
प्रातःसवनमादाय ऋत्विजः सर्व एव ते ..
स्वेस्वे कर्मणि संलग्ना यज्ञकृत्यसमुद्भवे .. 1 ..
5.183.m:
Sūta said:
When the third day arrived, on the thirteenth lunar day, O best of brahmins,
the sacrificial priests, undertaking the morning pressing of soma, all of them
engaged in their respective duties pertaining to the sacrificial acts.

5.183.s:
tataḥ pravartate yajñastadā paitāmaho mahān ..
sarvakāmasamṛddhastu sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ .. 2 ..
5.183.d:
ततः प्रवर्तते यज्ञस्तदा पैतामहो महान् ..
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्तु सर्वैः समुदितो गुणैः .. 2 ..
5.183.m:
Then proceeded that great sacrifice of the Grandfather,
rich in fulfilling all desires, accompanied by all excellences.

5.183.s:
dīyatāṃ dīyatāṃ tatra bhujyatāṃ bhujyatāmiti ..
ekaḥ saṃśrūyate śabdo dvitīyo dvijasaṃbhavaḥ .. 3 ..
5.183.d:
दीयतां दीयतां तत्र भुज्यतां भुज्यतामिति ..
एकः संश्रूयते शब्दो द्वितीयो द्विजसंभवः .. 3 ..
5.183.m:
“Let it be given! Let it be given! Eat! Eat!”—
this one sound was heard there; the second was the sound made by brahmins;

5.183.s:
nānyastatra tṛtīyastu yajñe paitāmahe śubhe ..
yo yaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ hemaratnasamudbhavam .. 4 ..
5.183.d:
नान्यस्तत्र तृतीयस्तु यज्ञे पैतामहे शुभे ..
यो यं कामयते कामं हेमरत्नसमुद्भवम् .. 4 ..
5.183.m:
there was no third [sound] in that auspicious sacrifice of the Grandfather.
Whatever desire one cherished, consisting of gold or gems,

5.183.s:
sa tatprāpnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ vāṃchitācca caturguṇam ..
pakvānnasya kṛtāstatra dṛśyaṃte parvatāḥ śubhāḥ .. 5 ..
5.183.d:
स तत्प्राप्नोत्यसंदिग्धं वांछिताच्च चतुर्गुणम् ..
पक्वान्नस्य कृतास्तत्र दृश्यंते पर्वताः शुभाः .. 5 ..
5.183.m:
one obtained it without a doubt, fourfold what was wished for.
Auspicious mountains made of cooked food were seen there,

5.183.s:
ghṛtakṣīra mahānadyo dānārthaṃ vittarāśayaḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare prāptaḥ kaścijjñānī dvijottamāḥ .. 6 ..
5.183.d:
घृतक्षीर महानद्यो दानार्थं वित्तराशयः ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तः कश्चिज्ज्ञानी द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6 ..
5.183.m:
and great rivers of ghee and milk, and heaps of wealth for donation.
At that moment, O best of brahmins, a certain wise man arrived,

5.183.s:
atītānāgatānvetti vartamānaṃ ca yaḥ sadā ..
sa brahmāṇaṃ namaskṛtya niviṣṭaśca tadagrataḥ .. 7 ..
5.183.d:
अतीतानागतान्वेत्ति वर्तमानं च यः सदा ..
स ब्रह्माणं नमस्कृत्य निविष्टश्च तदग्रतः .. 7 ..
5.183.m:
who always knew the past, the future, and the present.
Having bowed to Brahmā, he sat down before him.

5.183.s:
karmāṃtareṣu viprāṇāṃ sa sarveṣāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
kathayāmāsa yadvṛttaṃ bālyātprabhṛti kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 8 ..
5.183.d:
कर्मांतरेषु विप्राणां स सर्वेषां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
कथयामास यद्वृत्तं बाल्यात्प्रभृति कृत्स्नशः .. 8 ..
5.183.m:
During intervals between the rituals of the brahmins, O best of brahmins,
he recounted everything that had happened [to each of them] from childhood onwards.

5.183.s:
tatasta ṛtvijaḥ sarve kautukāviṣṭacetasaḥ ..
papracchurjñāninaṃ taṃ ca vismayotphullalocanāḥ .. 9 ..
5.183.d:
ततस्त ऋत्विजः सर्वे कौतुकाविष्टचेतसः ..
पप्रच्छुर्ज्ञानिनं तं च विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनाः .. 9 ..
5.183.m:
Then all those sacrificial priests, their minds filled with wonder,
and their eyes wide with amazement, questioned that wise man.

5.183.s:
vismṛtāni smaraṃtaste nijakṛtyāni vai tataḥ ..
proktāni garhaṇīyāni hyasaṃkhyātāni sarvaśaḥ .. 6.184.10 ..
5.183.d:
विस्मृतानि स्मरंतस्ते निजकृत्यानि वै ततः ..
प्रोक्तानि गर्हणीयानि ह्यसंख्यातानि सर्वशः .. 6.184.10 ..
5.183.m:
Remembering their own forgotten deeds,
innumerable and blameworthy in all respects, which he had spoken of,

5.183.s:
tataste punarevātha papracchurjñāninaṃ ca tam ..
lokottaramidaṃ jñānaṃ kathaṃ te saṃsthitaṃ dvija.. 11 ..
5.183.d:
ततस्ते पुनरेवाथ पप्रच्छुर्ज्ञानिनं च तम् ..
लोकोत्तरमिदं ज्ञानं कथं ते संस्थितं द्विज.. 11 ..
5.183.m:
they then questioned that wise man again:
“How did this extraordinary knowledge come to reside in you, O brahmin?

5.183.s:
ko guruste samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ..
ahojñānamaho jñānaṃ naitaddṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ ca na .. 12 ..
5.183.d:
को गुरुस्ते समाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि नः ..
अहोज्ञानमहो ज्ञानं नैतद्दृष्टं श्रुतं च न .. 12 ..
5.183.m:
Who is your guru? Tell us, for our curiosity is immense.
Ah, what knowledge! Ah, what knowledge! We have neither seen nor heard of such [knowledge],

5.183.s:
yādṛśaṃ te dvijaśreṣṭha dṛśyate pārthasaṃsthitam ..
kiṃ brahmaṇā svayaṃ vipra tvamevaṃ pratibodhitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.183.d:
यादृशं ते द्विजश्रेष्ठ दृश्यते पार्थसंस्थितम् ..
किं ब्रह्मणा स्वयं विप्र त्वमेवं प्रतिबोधितः .. 13 ..
5.183.m:
such as is seen dwelling in you, O best of brahmins, on this earth.
Were you thus awakened by Brahmā himself, O brahmin,

5.183.s:
kiṃ vā hareṇa tuṣṭena kiṃ vā devena cakriṇā ..
nānyaprabodhitasyaivaṃ jñānaṃ saṃjāyate sphuṭam .. 14 .. ..
5.183.d:
किं वा हरेण तुष्टेन किं वा देवेन चक्रिणा ..
नान्यप्रबोधितस्यैवं ज्ञानं संजायते स्फुटम् .. 14 .. ..
5.183.m:
or by pleased Hara, or by the discus-bearing God [Viṣṇu]?
Certainly, such knowledge cannot arise in one awakened by anyone else.”

5.183.s:
.. atithiruvāca .. ..
piṃgalā kuraraḥ sarpaḥ sāraṃgaścaiva yo vane ..
iṣukāraḥ kumārī ca ṣaḍete guravo mama .. 15 ..
5.183.d:
.. अतिथिरुवाच .. ..
पिंगला कुररः सर्पः सारंगश्चैव यो वने ..
इषुकारः कुमारी च षडेते गुरवो मम .. 15 ..
5.183.m:
The guest said:
“Piṅgalā, the osprey, the snake, the bee that wanders in the forest,
the arrow-maker, and the maiden: these six are my gurus.

5.183.s: eteṣāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā jñānaṃ me samupasthitam.. 16 ..
5.183.d: एतेषां चेष्टितं दृष्ट्वा ज्ञानं मे समुपस्थितम्.. 16 ..
5.183.m: Observing their behavior, knowledge arose in me.”

5.183.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
kathayasva mahābhāga kathaṃ te guravaḥ sthitāḥ ..
kīdṛśaṃ ca tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ teṣāṃ caiva viceṣṭitam .. .. 17 ..
5.183.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
कथयस्व महाभाग कथं ते गुरवः स्थिताः ..
कीदृशं च त्वया दृष्टं तेषां चैव विचेष्टितम् .. .. 17 ..
5.183.m:
The brahmins said:
“Tell us, O fortunate one, how they became your gurus,
and what conduct of theirs was observed by you?

5.183.s:
kasmindeśe tvamutpannaḥ kasminsthāne vadasva naḥ ..
kiṃnāmā kiṃ nu gotraśca sarvaṃ vistarato vada .. 18 ..
5.183.d:
कस्मिन्देशे त्वमुत्पन्नः कस्मिन्स्थाने वदस्व नः ..
किंनामा किं नु गोत्रश्च सर्वं विस्तरतो वद .. 18 ..
5.183.m:
In which country were you born? In what place? Tell us.
What is your name? What is your lineage? Tell us everything in detail.”

5.183.s:
.. atithiruvāca .. ..
āsannava pure viprāścatvāro ye vivāsitāḥ ..
śunaḥśepo'tha śākreyo bauddho dāṃtaścaturthakaḥ .. 19 ..
5.183.d:
.. अतिथिरुवाच .. ..
आसन्नव पुरे विप्राश्चत्वारो ये विवासिताः ..
शुनःशेपोऽथ शाक्रेयो बौद्धो दांतश्चतुर्थकः .. 19 ..
5.183.m:
The guest said:
“In the city of Navapura, there were four brahmins who had been banished:
Śunaḥśepa, Śākreya, Bauddha, and Dānta was the fourth.

5.183.s:
teṣāṃ madhye tu yo bauddhaḥ śāṃto dāṃta iti smṛtaḥ ..
chandogagotravikhyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 6.184.20 ..
5.183.d:
तेषां मध्ये तु यो बौद्धः शांतो दांत इति स्मृतः ..
छन्दोगगोत्रविख्यातो वेदवेदांगपारगः .. 6.184.20 ..
5.183.m:
Among them, he who was Bauddha was known as calm and self-restrained,
famous in the Chandoga gotra, a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

5.183.s:
nāgareṣu samutpannaḥ paścimevayasi sthitaḥ ..
tasyāhaṃ prathamaḥ putraḥ prāṇebhyo'pi suhṛtpriyaḥ .. 21 ..
5.183.d:
नागरेषु समुत्पन्नः पश्चिमेवयसि स्थितः ..
तस्याहं प्रथमः पुत्रः प्राणेभ्योऽपि सुहृत्प्रियः .. 21 ..
5.183.m:
born among the Nāgaras, and in the last stage of life.
I was his first son, dearer to him than his own life-breaths.

5.183.s:
tato'haṃ yauvanaṃ prāpto yadā dvijavarottama. ..
tadā me dayitastātaḥ paṃcatvaṃ samupāgataḥ .. 22 ..
5.183.d:
ततोऽहं यौवनं प्राप्तो यदा द्विजवरोत्तम. ..
तदा मे दयितस्तातः पंचत्वं समुपागतः .. 22 ..
5.183.m:
Then, when I attained youth, O best among the foremost brahmins,
my beloved father departed this life.

5.183.s:
etasminnaṃtare rājā hyānartādhipatirdvijāḥ ..
sutapāstena nirdiṣṭo'haṃ tu kaṃcukikarmaṇi .. 23 ..
5.183.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे राजा ह्यानर्ताधिपतिर्द्विजाः ..
सुतपास्तेन निर्दिष्टोऽहं तु कंचुकिकर्मणि .. 23 ..
5.183.m:
At that juncture, the king, the ruler of Ānarta, O brahmins,
[named] Sutapas, appointed me to the office of the chamberlain.

5.183.s:
śāṃtaṃ dāṃtaṃ samālokya viśvastena mahātmanā ..
tasya cāṃtaḥpure hyāsītpiṃgalānāma nāyikā .. 24 ..
5.183.d:
शांतं दांतं समालोक्य विश्वस्तेन महात्मना ..
तस्य चांतःपुरे ह्यासीत्पिंगलानाम नायिका .. 24 ..
5.183.m:
Seeing me calm and self-controlled, that noble one trusted me.
And in his inner apartment there was a courtesan named Piṅgalā,

5.183.s:
daurbhāgyeṇa samopetā rūpeṇāpi samanvitā ..
athānyāḥ śataśastasya bhāryāścāṃtaḥpure sthitāḥ .. 25 ..
5.183.d:
दौर्भाग्येण समोपेता रूपेणापि समन्विता ..
अथान्याः शतशस्तस्य भार्याश्चांतःपुरे स्थिताः .. 25 ..
5.183.m:
beset with misfortune, yet endowed with beauty.
Now, hundreds of his other wives stayed in the inner apartment;

5.183.s:
tāḥ sarvā rajanīvaktre vyākulatvaṃ prayāṃti ca ..
āharaṃti parāngandhāndhūpāṃśca kusumāni ca .. 26 ..
5.183.d:
ताः सर्वा रजनीवक्त्रे व्याकुलत्वं प्रयांति च ..
आहरंति परान्गन्धान्धूपांश्च कुसुमानि च .. 26 ..
5.183.m:
they all fell into agitation at nightfall,
bringing excellent perfumes, incenses, and flowers,

5.183.s:
vilepanāni mukhyāni surabhīṇi tathā puraḥ .. .
puṣpāṇi ca vicitrāṇi hyanyāḥ sūkṣmāṃbarāṇi ca ..27..
5.183.d:
विलेपनानि मुख्यानि सुरभीणि तथा पुरः .. .
पुष्पाणि च विचित्राणि ह्यन्याः सूक्ष्मांबराणि च ..27..
5.183.m:
and before [him] prominent, fragrant ointments,
and multicolored blossoms, while others brought fine garments,

5.183.s:
tāvadyāvatsthitaḥ kālaḥ śayanīyasamudbhavaḥ ..
manmathotsāhasaṃ yuktāḥ pulakena samanvitāḥ ..28..
5.183.d:
तावद्यावत्स्थितः कालः शयनीयसमुद्भवः ..
मन्मथोत्साहसं युक्ताः पुलकेन समन्विताः ..28..
5.183.m:
until the time for bed arrived,
filled with the excitement of desire and bristling with goosebumps.

5.183.s:
ekā jānāti māṃ suptāṃ nūnamākārayiṣyati ..
anyā jānāti māṃ caiva parasparamamarṣataḥ ..29..
5.183.d:
एका जानाति मां सुप्तां नूनमाकारयिष्यति ..
अन्या जानाति मां चैव परस्परममर्षतः ..29..
5.183.m:
One thinks, ‘Surely he will summon me who am asleep!’
Another thinks, ‘He will summon me!’—out of mutual jealousy,

5.183.s:
spardhayanti prayudhyanti virūpāṇi vadanti ca ..
tāsāṃ madhyāttataścaikā prayāti nṛpasaṃnidhau .. 6.184.30 ..
5.183.d:
स्पर्धयन्ति प्रयुध्यन्ति विरूपाणि वदन्ति च ..
तासां मध्यात्ततश्चैका प्रयाति नृपसंनिधौ .. 6.184.30 ..
5.183.m:
they rival, fight, and speak unpleasant words.
Then, from among them, one goes into the king's presence.

5.183.s:
śeṣā vai lakṣyamāsādya niḥśvasya prasvapanti ca ..
duḥkhārtā na labhanti sma tāśca nidrāṃ parābhavāt .. 31 ..
5.183.d:
शेषा वै लक्ष्यमासाद्य निःश्वस्य प्रस्वपन्ति च ..
दुःखार्ता न लभन्ति स्म ताश्च निद्रां पराभवात् .. 31 ..
5.183.m: The rest, failing to reach the mark, sighed and fell asleep; / afflicted with sorrow, they did not find sleep because of their humiliation.

5.183.s: kāmena pīḍitāṃgāśca bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇāḥ sthitāḥ .. 32 ..
5.183.d: कामेन पीडितांगाश्च बाष्पपूर्णेक्षणाः स्थिताः .. 32 ..
5.183.m: With limbs tormented by desire, they remained with eyes filled with tears.

5.183.s:
āśā hi paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ nirāśā paramaṃ sukham ..
āśānirāśāṃ kṛtvā ca sukhaṃ svapiti piṃgalā .. 33 ...
5.183.d:
आशा हि परमं दुःखं निराशा परमं सुखम् ..
आशानिराशां कृत्वा च सुखं स्वपिति पिंगला .. 33 ...
5.183.m: For expectation is supreme suffering, and freedom from expectation is supreme happiness. / Having turned expectation into freedom from expectation, Piṅgalā sleeps happily.

5.183.s:
na karoti ca śṛṃgāraṃ na spardhāṃ ca kadācana..
na vyākulatvamāpede sukhaṃ svapiti piṃgalā..34..
5.183.d:
न करोति च शृंगारं न स्पर्धां च कदाचन..
न व्याकुलत्वमापेदे सुखं स्वपिति पिंगला..34..
5.183.m: She makes no adornment, nor ever any rivalry; / she underwent no distress: Piṅgalā sleeps happily.

5.183.s:
tato mayāpi taddṛṣṭvā tasyāśceṣṭitamuttamam..
āśāḥ sarvāḥ parityaktāḥ svapimīha tataḥ sukhī..35..
5.183.d:
ततो मयापि तद्दृष्ट्वा तस्याश्चेष्टितमुत्तमम्..
आशाः सर्वाः परित्यक्ताः स्वपिमीह ततः सुखी..35..
5.183.m: Then, having seen that excellent conduct of hers, / I too abandoned all expectations, and therefore sleep here happily.

5.183.s:
ye svapaṃti sukhaṃ rātrau teṣāṃ kāyāgniridhyate.
āhāraṃ pratigṛhṇāti tataḥ puṣṭikaraṃ param..36..
5.183.d:
ये स्वपंति सुखं रात्रौ तेषां कायाग्निरिध्यते.
आहारं प्रतिगृह्णाति ततः पुष्टिकरं परम्..36..
5.183.m: For those who sleep happily at night, their bodily fire is kindled. / Then it receives food that gives the highest nourishment.

5.183.s:
tadetkāraṇaṃ jātaṃ mama tejo bhivṛddhaye..
gurutve piṃgalā jātā tena sā me dvijottamāḥ..37..
5.183.d:
तदेत्कारणं जातं मम तेजो भिवृद्धये..
गुरुत्वे पिंगला जाता तेन सा मे द्विजोत्तमाः..37..
5.183.m: That became the cause for the increase of my vigor. / Therefore, O best of brahmins, Piṅgalā became a guru to me.

5.183.s:
āśāpāśaiḥ parītāṃgā ye bhavanti naro rditāḥ..
te rātrau śerate naiva tadaprāptivicintayā..38..
5.183.d:
आशापाशैः परीतांगा ये भवन्ति नरो र्दिताः..
ते रात्रौ शेरते नैव तदप्राप्तिविचिन्तया..38..
5.183.m: Afflicted men whose limbs are bound by the snares of expectation / do not sleep at night, worrying over failing to attain it.

5.183.s:
naivāgnirdīpyate teṣāṃ jāṭharaśca tataḥ param..
āhāraṃ vāṃchate naiva tanna tejobhivardhanam..39..
5.183.d:
नैवाग्निर्दीप्यते तेषां जाठरश्च ततः परम्..
आहारं वांछते नैव तन्न तेजोभिवर्धनम्..39..
5.183.m: And their gastric fire does not burn beyond that; / they have no appetite for food, and thus there is no increase of vigor.

5.183.s: sarvasya vidyate prāṃto na vāṃchāyāḥ kathaṃcana..6.184.40..
5.183.d: सर्वस्य विद्यते प्रांतो न वांछायाः कथंचन..6.184.40..
5.183.m: Everything has a limit, but desire has none whatever.

5.183.s:
yathāyathā bhavellābho vāṃcitasya nṛṇāmiha..
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva vṛddhiṃ yāti tathātathā..41..
5.183.d:
यथायथा भवेल्लाभो वांचितस्य नृणामिह..
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव वृद्धिं याति तथातथा..41..
5.183.m: In whatever manner the attainment of the desired thing happens for men here, / in that very manner it grows, like fire fed with clarified butter.

5.183.s:
yathā śṛṃgaṃ ruroḥ kāye vardhamānasya vardhate..
evaṃ tṛṣṇāpi yatnena vardhamānena vardhate..42..
5.183.d:
यथा शृंगं रुरोः काये वर्धमानस्य वर्धते..
एवं तृष्णापि यत्नेन वर्धमानेन वर्धते..42..
5.183.m: Just as the horn of a ruru deer grows on its growing body, / so also thirst [of desire] grows with growing exertion.

5.183.s:
evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāgaḥ puruṣeṇa vijānatā..
divā tatkarma kartavyaṃ yena rātrau sukhaṃ svapet..43..
5.183.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा महाभागः पुरुषेण विजानता..
दिवा तत्कर्म कर्तव्यं येन रात्रौ सुखं स्वपेत्..43..
5.183.m: Knowing thus, O fortunate one, by a discerning man / that deed must be done by day whereby he may sleep happily at night.

5.183.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye brahmayajñe tṛtīyadivase piṃgalopākhyānavarṇanaṃnāma caturaśītyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..184..
5.183.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मयज्ञे तृतीयदिवसे पिंगलोपाख्यानवर्णनंनाम चतुरशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः..184..
5.183.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-fourth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Story of Piṅgalā on the Third Day of the Brahmayajña,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Mahāpurāṇa of Skanda, consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.184.s:
atithiruvāca..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā me piṃgalā guruḥ..
saṃjātā kuraro jāto yathā tatpravadānyaham..1..
5.184.d:
अतिथिरुवाच..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यथा मे पिंगला गुरुः..
संजाता कुररो जातो यथा तत्प्रवदान्यहम्..1..
5.184.m: The guest said: / All this has been related to you, how Piṅgalā became my guru. / How the osprey became [my guru], that I will tell.

5.184.s: mamāsīddraviṇaṃ bhūri pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat..2..
5.184.d: ममासीद्द्रविणं भूरि पितृपैतामहं महत्..2..
5.184.m: I had great wealth, abundant and ancestral.

5.184.s:
ye'tha putrāśca dāyādā bāṃdhavā api..
te māṃ sarve prabādhante dravyasasyakṛte sadā..3..
5.184.d:
येऽथ पुत्राश्च दायादा बांधवा अपि..
ते मां सर्वे प्रबाधन्ते द्रव्यसस्यकृते सदा..3..
5.184.m: The sons, heirs, and relatives who were there— / all of them constantly tormented me for the sake of the wealth of crops.

5.184.s:
yasyāhaṃ na prayacchāmi sa māṃ caiva prabādhate..
sīdamānastu subhṛśaṃ darśayanprāṇasaṃkṣayam..4..
5.184.d:
यस्याहं न प्रयच्छामि स मां चैव प्रबाधते..
सीदमानस्तु सुभृशं दर्शयन्प्राणसंक्षयम्..4..
5.184.m: Whomever I did not give to, he harassed me, / sinking into deep despair and displaying the loss of his life.

5.184.s:
eka sāmnā prayācaṃte vittaṃ bhedena cāpare ..
bhayadānena cānye'pi keciddaṃḍena ca dvijāḥ .. 5 ..
5.184.d:
एक साम्ना प्रयाचंते वित्तं भेदेन चापरे ..
भयदानेन चान्येऽपि केचिद्दंडेन च द्विजाः .. 5 ..
5.184.m: Some begged for wealth with gentle words, and others by creating division; / yet others with threats of danger, and some with punishment, O brahmins.

5.184.s:
evaṃ nāhaṃ kvacitsaukhyaṃ teṣāṃ pārśvāllabhāmi bhoḥ ..
cintayāno divānaktaṃ kleśasya pari saṃkṣayam ..
upāyaṃ na ca paśyāmi yena śāṃtiḥ prajāyate .. 6 ..
5.184.d:
एवं नाहं क्वचित्सौख्यं तेषां पार्श्वाल्लभामि भोः ..
चिन्तयानो दिवानक्तं क्लेशस्य परि संक्षयम् ..
उपायं न च पश्यामि येन शांतिः प्रजायते .. 6 ..
5.184.m: Thus I found no happiness anywhere by their side, O sirs! / Pondering day and night the complete cessation of my distress, / I saw no means whereby peace could arise.

5.184.s:
anyasmindivase dṛṣṭaḥ kṛtamāṃsaparigrahaḥ ..
kuraraścaṃcunā vyomni gacchamānastvarānvitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.184.d:
अन्यस्मिन्दिवसे दृष्टः कृतमांसपरिग्रहः ..
कुररश्चंचुना व्योम्नि गच्छमानस्त्वरान्वितः .. 7 ..
5.184.m: On another day, an osprey was seen, holding meat in its beak, / flying through the sky in haste,

5.184.s:
hanyamānaḥ samaṃtācca māṃsārthe vividhaiḥ khagaiḥ ..
atha tena parikṣiptaṃ tanmāṃsaṃ pakṣijādbhayāt .. 8 ..
5.184.d:
हन्यमानः समंताच्च मांसार्थे विविधैः खगैः ..
अथ तेन परिक्षिप्तं तन्मांसं पक्षिजाद्भयात् .. 8 ..
5.184.m: being struck on all sides by various birds for the sake of the meat. / Then it dropped that meat out of fear of the birds.

5.184.s:
yāvattāvatsukhī jātaste'pisarve samujjhitāḥ ..
mayāpi kliśyamānena tadvacca nijabāṃdhavaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.184.d:
यावत्तावत्सुखी जातस्तेऽपिसर्वे समुज्झिताः ..
मयापि क्लिश्यमानेन तद्वच्च निजबांधवैः .. 9 ..
5.184.m: In that very instant it became happy, and all [the birds] departed. / By me too, afflicted in the same manner by my own relatives,

5.184.s:
sāmiṣaṃ kuraraṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ nirāmiṣaiḥ ..
āmiṣasya parityāgātkuraraḥ sukhamedhate .. 6.185.10 ..
5.184.d:
सामिषं कुररं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं निरामिषैः ..
आमिषस्य परित्यागात्कुररः सुखमेधते .. 6.185.10 ..
5.184.m: having seen the osprey with meat being struck by those without meat, / [I realized]: through the abandonment of the meat, the osprey thrives in happiness.

5.184.s:
evaṃ niścitya manasā sarvānānīya bāṃdhavān ..
putrānpautrāṃstataḥ sarvānpurasteṣāṃ niveditam .. 11 ..
5.184.d:
एवं निश्चित्य मनसा सर्वानानीय बांधवान् ..
पुत्रान्पौत्रांस्ततः सर्वान्पुरस्तेषां निवेदितम् .. 11 ..
5.184.m: Deciding thus in my mind, I brought together all my relatives, / and then all my sons and grandsons, and declared before them:

5.184.s:
triḥsatyaṃ śapathaṃ kṛtvā nānyadastīti me gṛhe ..
vibhajyārthaṃ yathānyāyaṃ yūyaṃ gṛhṇīta bāndhavāḥ .. 12 ..
5.184.d:
त्रिःसत्यं शपथं कृत्वा नान्यदस्तीति मे गृहे ..
विभज्यार्थं यथान्यायं यूयं गृह्णीत बान्धवाः .. 12 ..
5.184.m: "Taking an oath three times truthfully: there is nothing else in my house. / Dividing the property according to rule, take it, O relatives!"

5.184.s:
tataḥprabhṛti tairmuktaḥ sukhaṃ tiṣṭhāmyahaṃ dvijāḥ ..
etasmātkāraṇājjāto mamāsau kuraro guruḥ.. 13 ..
5.184.d:
ततःप्रभृति तैर्मुक्तः सुखं तिष्ठाम्यहं द्विजाः ..
एतस्मात्कारणाज्जातो ममासौ कुररो गुरुः.. 13 ..
5.184.m: From then on, released by them, I dwell happily, O brahmins. / For this reason, that osprey became my guru.

5.184.s:
arthasaṃpadvimohāya vimoho narakāya ca ..
tasmādarthamanarthaṃ taṃ mokṣārthī dūratastyajet .. 14 ..
5.184.d:
अर्थसंपद्विमोहाय विमोहो नरकाय च ..
तस्मादर्थमनर्थं तं मोक्षार्थी दूरतस्त्यजेत् .. 14 ..
5.184.m: Abundance of wealth leads to delusion, and delusion leads to hell. / Therefore, one who seeks liberation should abandon that wealth, which is misfortune, from afar.

5.184.s:
yathāmiṣaṃ jale matsyairbhakṣyate śvāpadairbhuvi..
ākāśe pakṣibhiścaiva tathā sarvatra vittavān..15..
5.184.d:
यथामिषं जले मत्स्यैर्भक्ष्यते श्वापदैर्भुवि..
आकाशे पक्षिभिश्चैव तथा सर्वत्र वित्तवान्..15..
5.184.m: Just as meat is devoured by fish in water, by wild beasts on earth, / and by birds in the sky, so is a wealthy man everywhere.

5.184.s:
doṣahīno'pi dhanavānbhūpādyaiḥ paritāpyate..
daridraḥ kṛtadoṣo'pi sarvatra nirupadravaḥ..16..
5.184.d:
दोषहीनोऽपि धनवान्भूपाद्यैः परिताप्यते..
दरिद्रः कृतदोषोऽपि सर्वत्र निरुपद्रवः..16..
5.184.m: Even a blameless rich man is harassed by kings and others; / a poor man, even if he has committed a fault, is unmolested everywhere.

5.184.s:
ālaṃbitāḥ parairyāṃti praskhalaṃti padepade ..
gadgadāni ca jalpaṃte dhanino madyapā iva..17..
5.184.d:
आलंबिताः परैर्यांति प्रस्खलंति पदेपदे ..
गद्गदानि च जल्पंते धनिनो मद्यपा इव..17..
5.184.m: Supported by others, stumbling at every step, / they babble falteringly—the wealthy, like drunkards.

5.184.s:
bhakte dveṣo bahiḥ prītī rucitaṃ gurulaghvapi ..
mukhe ca kaṭutā nityaṃ dhanināṃ jvariṇāmiva ..18..
5.184.d:
भक्ते द्वेषो बहिः प्रीती रुचितं गुरुलघ्वपि ..
मुखे च कटुता नित्यं धनिनां ज्वरिणामिव ..18..
5.184.m: Hatred toward the devoted, outward affection, appetite fickle for heavy or light, / and constant bitterness in the mouth—of the rich, like people with fever.

5.184.s:
arthānāmarjane duḥkhamarjitānāṃ ca rakṣaṇe ..
nāśe duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhaṃ dhigartho duḥkhabhājanam..19..
5.184.d:
अर्थानामर्जने दुःखमर्जितानां च रक्षणे ..
नाशे दुःखं व्यये दुःखं धिगर्थो दुःखभाजनम्..19..
5.184.m: There is suffering in earning wealth, and in guarding what has been earned; / there is suffering in its loss, suffering in its expenditure: fie upon wealth, a vessel of suffering!

5.184.s:
arthārthī jīva loko'yaṃ smaśānamapi sevate ..
janitāramapi tyaktvā niḥsvaṃ yāṃti sutā api .. 6.185.20 ..
5.184.d:
अर्थार्थी जीव लोकोऽयं स्मशानमपि सेवते ..
जनितारमपि त्यक्त्वा निःस्वं यांति सुता अपि .. 6.185.20 ..
5.184.m: Seeking wealth, this world of living beings serves even the cremation ground; / leaving even their progenitor destitute, even sons depart.

5.184.s:
sutasya vallabhastāvatpitā putro'pi vai pituḥ ..
yāvannārthasya saṃbandhastābhyāṃ bhāvī parasparam ..
saṃbandhe vittaje jāte vairaṃ saṃjāyate mithaḥ .. 21 ..
5.184.d:
सुतस्य वल्लभस्तावत्पिता पुत्रोऽपि वै पितुः ..
यावन्नार्थस्य संबन्धस्ताभ्यां भावी परस्परम् ..
संबन्धे वित्तजे जाते वैरं संजायते मिथः .. 21 ..
5.184.m: A father is dear to a son, and a son to a father, / only as long as there is to be no dealing of wealth between the two; / when a relation arisen from wealth occurs, mutual enmity arises.

5.184.s:
etasmātkāraṇādvittaṃ mayā tyaktaṃ tapodhanāḥ ..
tena saukhyena tiṣṭhāmi kurarasyopadeśataḥ .. 22 ..
5.184.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्वित्तं मया त्यक्तं तपोधनाः ..
तेन सौख्येन तिष्ठामि कुररस्योपदेशतः .. 22 ..
5.184.m: For this reason, wealth was abandoned by me, O you rich in asceticism. / Therefore I dwell in happiness, through the instruction of the osprey.

5.184.s: śṛṇudhvaṃ ca mahābhāgā yathā me'hirguruḥ sthitaḥ .. 23 ..
5.184.d: शृणुध्वं च महाभागा यथा मेऽहिर्गुरुः स्थितः .. 23 ..
5.184.m: And listen, O fortunate ones, how the serpent was my guru,

5.184.s:
yathā mayā gṛhaṃ tyaktaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam ..
gṛhāraṃbhaḥ suduḥkhāya sukhāya na kadācana .. 24 ..
5.184.d:
यथा मया गृहं त्यक्तं दृष्ट्वा सर्पविचेष्टितम् ..
गृहारंभः सुदुःखाय सुखाय न कदाचन .. 24 ..
5.184.m: how I abandoned home having seen the conduct of the serpent. / Undertaking a household leads to great suffering, never to happiness.

5.184.s:
sarpaḥ parakṛtaṃ veśma praviśya sukhamedhate ..
uṣitvā tatra saukhyena bhūyo'nyattādṛśaṃ vrajet .. 25 ..
5.184.d:
सर्पः परकृतं वेश्म प्रविश्य सुखमेधते ..
उषित्वा तत्र सौख्येन भूयोऽन्यत्तादृशं व्रजेत् .. 25 ..
5.184.m: Entering a dwelling made by another, the serpent thrives in happiness; / having dwelt there pleasantly, it moves again to another such.

5.184.s:
mama tvaṃ kurute naiva mamedaṃ gṛhamityasau ..
na gṛhaṃ jāyate tasya na svayaṃ hi kṛtaṃ yataḥ .. 26 ..
5.184.d:
मम त्वं कुरुते नैव ममेदं गृहमित्यसौ ..
न गृहं जायते तस्य न स्वयं हि कृतं यतः .. 26 ..
5.184.m: It never makes the sense of 'mine' saying: 'This is my home.' / No house belongs to it, because it did not build one itself.

5.184.s:
yaḥ punaḥ kurute harmyaṃ svayaṃ kleśaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ ..
na tasya yāti tatpaścānmṛtyukāle'pi saṃsthite .. 27 ..
5.184.d:
यः पुनः कुरुते हर्म्यं स्वयं क्लेशैः पृथग्विधैः ..
न तस्य याति तत्पश्चान्मृत्युकालेऽपि संस्थिते .. 27 ..
5.184.m: He, however, who builds a mansion himself with various troubles, / that does not follow him after death, even when he has departed.

5.184.s:
gṛhātsaṃjāyate bhāryā tataḥ putraśca kanyakā ..
teṣāmarthe karoti sma kṛtyākṛtyaṃ tataḥ param ..28..
5.184.d:
गृहात्संजायते भार्या ततः पुत्रश्च कन्यका ..
तेषामर्थे करोति स्म कृत्याकृत्यं ततः परम् ..28..
5.184.m: From a home arises a wife, and then a son and a daughter; / for their sake he then commits what should and should not be done.

5.184.s:
kośakāramivātmānaṃ veṣṭayannāvabudhyate ..129 ..
putradāragṛhakṣetrasaktāḥ sīdaṃti jaṃtavaḥ ..
lobhapaṃkārṇave magnā jīrṇā vanagajā iva .. 6.185.30 ..
ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṃkte mahājanaḥ ..
bhoktāro vipramucyaṃte kartā doṣeṇa lipyate 31 ..
etasmātkāraṇāddharmyaṃ mayā tyaktaṃ dvijottamāḥ.
mokṣamārgārgalā bhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam .. 32 ..
ekarātraṃ vasedgrāme trirātraṃ pattane vaset ..
yo yāti sa yatiḥ prokto yo'nyo yogaviḍaṃbakaḥ .. 33 ..
vidhūme ca praśāṃtāgnau yastu mādhukarīṃ caret ..
gṛhe ca vipramukhyānāṃ yatiḥ sa netaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 34 ..
daṇḍī bhikṣāṃ ca vā kuryāttadeva vyasanaṃ vinā ..
yastiṣṭhati na vairāgyaṃ yāti naiva yatirhi saḥ .. 35 ..
divā svapnaṃ vṛthānnaṃ ca strīkathā''lokyameva ca ..
śvetavastraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca yatīnāṃ patanāni ṣaṭ.. 36..
5.184.d:
कोशकारमिवात्मानं वेष्टयन्नावबुध्यते ..129 ..
पुत्रदारगृहक्षेत्रसक्ताः सीदंति जंतवः ..
लोभपंकार्णवे मग्ना जीर्णा वनगजा इव .. 6.185.30 ..
एकः पापानि कुरुते फलं भुंक्ते महाजनः ..
भोक्तारो विप्रमुच्यंते कर्ता दोषेण लिप्यते 31 ..
एतस्मात्कारणाद्धर्म्यं मया त्यक्तं द्विजोत्तमाः.
मोक्षमार्गार्गला भूतं दृष्ट्वा सर्पविचेष्टितम् .. 32 ..
एकरात्रं वसेद्ग्रामे त्रिरात्रं पत्तने वसेत् ..
यो याति स यतिः प्रोक्तो योऽन्यो योगविडंबकः .. 33 ..
विधूमे च प्रशांताग्नौ यस्तु माधुकरीं चरेत् ..
गृहे च विप्रमुख्यानां यतिः स नेतरः स्मृतः .. 34 ..
दण्डी भिक्षां च वा कुर्यात्तदेव व्यसनं विना ..
यस्तिष्ठति न वैराग्यं याति नैव यतिर्हि सः .. 35 ..
दिवा स्वप्नं वृथान्नं च स्त्रीकथा'ऽलोक्यमेव च ..
श्वेतवस्त्रं हिरण्यं च यतीनां पतनानि षट्.. 36..
5.184.m:
Enveloping himself like a silkworm, he does not understand.
Attached to sons, wives, houses, and fields, living beings sink down, / drowned in an ocean-mire of greed, like decrepit wild elephants.
One man commits sins; the multitude enjoys the fruit. / The enjoyers are freed, but the doer is tainted by the fault.
For this reason, O best of brahmins, I abandoned [household] duty / having seen the behavior of a snake, which was an obstacle on the path to liberation. 32
He should stay one night in a village, and three nights in a city. / He who wanders thus is called an ascetic; anyone else is a mocker of yoga. 33
He who wanders for bee-like alms when smoke has ceased and fires are extinguished, / and in the houses of the foremost brahmins—he is remembered as an ascetic, not another. 34
Carrying a staff, he should beg alms, without that very vice [of clinging]; / he who remains, but does not attain dispassion, is certainly no ascetic. 35
Sleeping by day, useless food, conversation about women, gazing [at them], / white garments, and gold: these are the six downfalls of ascetics. 36

5.184.s:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanaḥ ..
suhṛtputra udāsīnaḥ sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 37 ..
samau mānāpamānau ca svadeśe parikepi vā ..
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 38 ..
yasmingṛhe viśeṣeṇa labhedbhikṣā ca vāśanam ..
tatra no yāti yo bhūyaḥ sa yatirnetaraḥ smṛtaḥ. .. 39 ..
evaṃ jñātvā mayā vipra dṛṣṭvā sarpaviceṣṭitam ..
sarvasaṃgaparityāgo mokṣārthaṃ parikalpitaḥ .. 6.185.40 ..
evaṃ mamāhiḥ saṃjāto gururbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ.
tatprabhāvānmahattejaḥ saṃjātaṃ vigrahe mama .. 41 ..
yathā me bhramaro jāto gurustadvadvadāmi ca ..
kasminvṛkṣe mayā dṛṣṭo bhramaraḥ ko'pi saṃgataḥ ..42..
śākhāya tu samāśritya kṛtapūrvanibaṃdhanam ..
vasaṃtasamaye prāpte puṣpavaṃtaśca ye drumāḥ .. 43 ..
5.184.d:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च समलोष्टाश्मकांचनः ..
सुहृत्पुत्र उदासीनः स यतिर्नेतरः स्मृतः .. 37 ..
समौ मानापमानौ च स्वदेशे परिकेपि वा ..
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि स यतिर्नेतरः स्मृतः .. 38 ..
यस्मिन्गृहे विशेषेण लभेद्भिक्षा च वाशनम् ..
तत्र नो याति यो भूयः स यतिर्नेतरः स्मृतः. .. 39 ..
एवं ज्ञात्वा मया विप्र दृष्ट्वा सर्पविचेष्टितम् ..
सर्वसंगपरित्यागो मोक्षार्थं परिकल्पितः .. 6.185.40 ..
एवं ममाहिः संजातो गुरुर्ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः.
तत्प्रभावान्महत्तेजः संजातं विग्रहे मम .. 41 ..
यथा मे भ्रमरो जातो गुरुस्तद्वद्वदामि च ..
कस्मिन्वृक्षे मया दृष्टो भ्रमरः कोऽपि संगतः ..42..
शाखाय तु समाश्रित्य कृतपूर्वनिबंधनम् ..
वसंतसमये प्राप्ते पुष्पवंतश्च ये द्रुमाः .. 43 ..
5.184.m:
Equal toward enemy and friend, viewing a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal, / indifferent toward a friend or a son: he is remembered as an ascetic, not another. 37
Equal in honor and dishonor, whether in his own land or abroad, / he who neither rejoices nor hates: he is remembered as an ascetic, not another. 38
In whichever house he receives special alms or food, / he who does not go there again: he is remembered as an ascetic, not another. 39
Having understood this, O brahmin, and having seen the behavior of the snake, / the abandonment of all attachments was resolved upon by me for the sake of liberation. 40
In this way the serpent became my guru, O best of brahmins; / by its power, great splendor arose in my body. 41
I shall also tell how the black bee became my guru: / in a certain tree, a certain black bee was seen by me as it arrived. 42
Resorting to a branch, it made its previous dwelling. / When the spring season arrived, and the trees were in bloom, 43

5.184.s:
sugandhaphalapuṣpāśca sugandhadalasaṃyutāḥ ..
teṣāmaṇuṃ samādāya śreṣṭhaśreṣṭhatamaṃ rasam .. 44 .
niyojayati śākhāgre tarorasya sadaiva hi ..
anirviṇṇatayā hṛṣṭastadā samyaṅnirīkṣitaḥ .. 45 ..
madhujālaṃ tato jātaṃ kālena mahatā mahat ..
yenānye madhunā tṛptiṃ prāptāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ .. 46 ..
tacceṣṭitaṃ mayā vīkṣya śāstrāṇyanyāni bhūriśaḥ ..
tatasteṣāṃ samādāya sārabhūtaṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
kṛtāni bhūriśāstrāṇi vedāṃtāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 47 ..
upajīvaṃti yānyanye yathā bhṛṅgāstathā dvijāḥ .. 48 ..
evaṃ me madhupo jāto gurutve ca dvijottamāḥ ..
tenāhaṃ tejasā yukto nānyadastīha kāraṇam.. 49 ..
vedāṃtavādino ye'tra prabhavaṃti vratānvitāḥ ..
nirlobhā gatatṛṣṇāśca te bhavaṃti sutejasaḥ .. 6.185.50 ..
ekenāpi vihīnā ye prabhavaṃti kubuddhayaḥ ..
lobhamohānvitāḥ pāpā jāyaṃte te vicetasaḥ ..51..
5.184.d:
सुगन्धफलपुष्पाश्च सुगन्धदलसंयुताः ..
तेषामणुं समादाय श्रेष्ठश्रेष्ठतमं रसम् .. 44 .
नियोजयति शाखाग्रे तरोरस्य सदैव हि ..
अनिर्विण्णतया हृष्टस्तदा सम्यङ्निरीक्षितः .. 45 ..
मधुजालं ततो जातं कालेन महता महत् ..
येनान्ये मधुना तृप्तिं प्राप्ताः शतसहस्रशः .. 46 ..
तच्चेष्टितं मया वीक्ष्य शास्त्राण्यन्यानि भूरिशः ..
ततस्तेषां समादाय सारभूतं पृथक्पृथक् ..
कृतानि भूरिशास्त्राणि वेदांतानि च कृत्स्नशः .. 47 ..
उपजीवंति यान्यन्ये यथा भृङ्गास्तथा द्विजाः .. 48 ..
एवं मे मधुपो जातो गुरुत्वे च द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तेनाहं तेजसा युक्तो नान्यदस्तीह कारणम्.. 49 ..
वेदांतवादिनो येऽत्र प्रभवंति व्रतान्विताः ..
निर्लोभा गततृष्णाश्च ते भवंति सुतेजसः .. 6.185.50 ..
एकेनापि विहीना ये प्रभवंति कुबुद्धयः ..
लोभमोहान्विताः पापा जायंते ते विचेतसः ..51..
5.184.m:
bearing fragrant fruits and blossoms, and endowed with fragrant leaves, / taking an atom from them, the finest and most excellent nectar, 44
it always deposited it at the tip of a branch of that tree; / joyful and untiring, it was then carefully observed [by me]. 45
Then, after a great deal of time, a great honeycomb was formed, / through which honey hundreds and thousands of others obtained satisfaction. 46
Having observed that activity, and [studying] numerous other scriptures, / having extracted the essential core from them separately, / numerous treatises and Vedānta texts were composed in full [by me], 47
which others—just as bees [live on honey]—the brahmins live upon. 48
Thus the honey-drinker became a guru to me, O best of brahmins; / endowed with that splendor, I [live]; there is no other reason here. 49
Those Vedānta teachers who arise here, endowed with vows, / free from greed, and devoid of thirst—they become full of great splendor. 50
Those of evil intellect who arise lacking even one [of these virtues], / filled with greed and delusion, sinful, they become senseless. 51

5.184.s:
vedāṃtāni subhūrīṇi mayā dṛṣṭvā vicārya ca ..
samarūpāḥ kṛtā granthā martyalokahitārthinā .. 52 ..
evaṃ me gurutāṃ prāpto madhupo dvijasattamāḥ ..
iṣukāro yathā jātastathā caiva bravīmi vaḥ..53..
ātmāvalokanārthāya mayā dṛṣṭāḥ sahasraśaḥ..
yogino jñānasaṃpannāstaiḥ proktaṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ..54..
ātmāvalokanaṃ bhāvi suśiṣyāya yathā tathā..
sa samādhijadvāreṇa caturāśītikena ca..55..
āsanaistatpramāṇaiśca padmāsanaprapūrvakaiḥ..
asaṃkhyaiḥ kāraṇaiścaiva hyadhyātmapaṭhanaistathā..
tatopi lakṣito naiva mayā'tmā ca kathaṃcana..56..
tato vairāgyamāpannaḥ prabhramāmi dharātale..
gurvarthe na ca lebhe'haṃ gurumātmāvalokane .. 57 ..
anyasminnahani prāpte rājamārgeṇa gacchatā ..
mayā dṛṣṭo mahīpālaḥ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ .. 58 ..
5.184.d:
वेदांतानि सुभूरीणि मया दृष्ट्वा विचार्य च ..
समरूपाः कृता ग्रन्था मर्त्यलोकहितार्थिना .. 52 ..
एवं मे गुरुतां प्राप्तो मधुपो द्विजसत्तमाः ..
इषुकारो यथा जातस्तथा चैव ब्रवीमि वः..53..
आत्मावलोकनार्थाय मया दृष्टाः सहस्रशः..
योगिनो ज्ञानसंपन्नास्तैः प्रोक्तं च स्वशक्तितः..54..
आत्मावलोकनं भावि सुशिष्याय यथा तथा..
स समाधिजद्वारेण चतुराशीतिकेन च..55..
आसनैस्तत्प्रमाणैश्च पद्मासनप्रपूर्वकैः..
असंख्यैः कारणैश्चैव ह्यध्यात्मपठनैस्तथा..
ततोपि लक्षितो नैव मयाऽत्मा च कथंचन..56..
ततो वैराग्यमापन्नः प्रभ्रमामि धरातले..
गुर्वर्थे न च लेभेऽहं गुरुमात्मावलोकने .. 57 ..
अन्यस्मिन्नहनि प्राप्ते राजमार्गेण गच्छता ..
मया दृष्टो महीपालः सैन्येन महता वृतः .. 58 ..
5.184.m:
Having seen and reflected upon numerous Vedāntas, / treatises of equal nature were composed by me, desiring the welfare of the mortal world. 52
Thus the honey-drinker attained guruship for me, O best of brahmins; / I shall also tell you how the arrow-maker became [my guru]. 53
In order to perceive the self, thousands of yogins endowed with knowledge / were seen by me, and they spoke according to their own capacity: 54
‘Perception of the self will occur for a good disciple in this manner: / through the gateway born of samādhi, and through the eighty-four 55
postures of that measure, beginning with the lotus posture, / through countless methods, and through study of spiritual philosophy.’ / Even so, the self was not perceived by me at all. 56
Then, having attained dispassion, I wandered about the earth / in search of a guru, yet I did not find a guru for the perception of the self. 57
When another day arrived, as I walked along the royal highway, / a king surrounded by a vast army was seen by me. 58

5.184.s:
tato'haṃ mārgamutsṛjya saṃmukhasya mahīpateḥ ..
uṭajadvāramāśritya kiṃcidūrdhvopi saṃsthitaḥ .. 59 ..
tatrāpi ca sthitaḥ kaścitpuruṣaḥ kāṃḍakārakaḥ ..
ṛjukarmaṇi saṃyuktaḥ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām.. 6.185.60 ..
tasmindūragate bhūpe tathānyaḥ sevako'bhyagāt .. 61 ..
taṃ papraccha tvarāyuktaḥ śṛṇvato'pi mama dvijāḥ ..
kāṃḍakarmaṇi saṃsaktamṛjutvena sthitaṃ tadā ..62..
kiyatī vartate velā gatasya pṛthivīpateḥ ..
mārgeṇānena me brūhi yena gacchāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ..63..
so'bravīttaṃ tadā viprā adhovaktraḥ sthito naraḥ ..
anena rājamārgeṇa gacchamāno mahīpatiḥ .. 64 ..
na mayā vīkṣitaḥ kaścididānīṃ rājasevaka ..
tadanyaṃ pṛccha cetkāryaṃ tavānena bravītu saḥ .. 65 ..
śarakarmaṇi saṃsaktastvahamatra vyavasthitaḥ ..
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya svacitte cintitaṃ mayā..66..
5.184.d:
ततोऽहं मार्गमुत्सृज्य संमुखस्य महीपतेः ..
उटजद्वारमाश्रित्य किंचिदूर्ध्वोपि संस्थितः .. 59 ..
तत्रापि च स्थितः कश्चित्पुरुषः कांडकारकः ..
ऋजुकर्मणि संयुक्तः शराणां नतपर्वणाम्.. 6.185.60 ..
तस्मिन्दूरगते भूपे तथान्यः सेवकोऽभ्यगात् .. 61 ..
तं पप्रच्छ त्वरायुक्तः शृण्वतोऽपि मम द्विजाः ..
कांडकर्मणि संसक्तमृजुत्वेन स्थितं तदा ..62..
कियती वर्तते वेला गतस्य पृथिवीपतेः ..
मार्गेणानेन मे ब्रूहि येन गच्छामि पृष्ठतः..63..
सोऽब्रवीत्तं तदा विप्रा अधोवक्त्रः स्थितो नरः ..
अनेन राजमार्गेण गच्छमानो महीपतिः .. 64 ..
न मया वीक्षितः कश्चिदिदानीं राजसेवक ..
तदन्यं पृच्छ चेत्कार्यं तवानेन ब्रवीतु सः .. 65 ..
शरकर्मणि संसक्तस्त्वहमत्र व्यवस्थितः ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य स्वचित्ते चिन्तितं मया..66..
5.184.m:
Then, stepping off the path from facing the king, / I stood slightly elevated, taking shelter at the entrance of a hut. 59
There also stood a certain man, a maker of shafts, / engaged in the work of straightening arrows with curved joints. 60
When that king had gone far off, another servant approached. 61
Filled with haste, even while I was listening, O brahmins, he asked him / who was intent on the work of shafts, absorbed at that time in straightening: 62
‘How long has it been since the lord of the earth departed / by this road? Tell me, so that I may go after him.’ 63
That man, standing with his face downward, then said to him, O brahmins: / ‘A king passing along this royal highway 64
was not seen by me just now, O king’s servant. / Therefore ask another; if you have business with him, let him tell you. 65
I am standing here wholly intent upon the work of arrows.’ / Hearing that speech of his, it was contemplated by me in my own mind: 66

5.184.s:
ekacittatayā yogo brahmajñānasamudbhavaḥ ..
nānyathā bhavitā me sa tataścittanirodhanam ..
karomi brahmasaṃsiddhyai tato me'sau bhaviṣyati .. 67 ..
tataḥprabhṛti citte sve dhārayāmi sadaiva tu ..
viśvarūpaṃ tathā sūryaṃ hṛtpaṃkajanivāsinam .. 68 ..
tato dikṣu diganteṣu gagane dharaṇītale ..
tamekaṃ caiva paśyāmi nānyatkiṃciddvijottamāḥ .. 69 ..
ahaṃ ca tejasā yuktastatprabhāveṇa saṃsthitaḥ .. 6.185.70 ..
evaṃ me sa gururjātaḥ śarakāro dvijottamāḥ ..
śṛṇudhvaṃ kanyakā jātā gurutve me yathā purā .. 71 ..
sarvasaṃgaparityāgī yadāhaṃ nirgato gṛhāt ..
mamānupṛṣṭhataścaiva tato bhāryā vinirgatā .. 72 ..
śiśuṃ putraṃ samādāya kanyāmekāṃ ca śobhanām..
tato'haṃ bhāryayā prokto vānaprasthāśrame sthitaḥ..73..
5.184.d:
एकचित्ततया योगो ब्रह्मज्ञानसमुद्भवः ..
नान्यथा भविता मे स ततश्चित्तनिरोधनम् ..
करोमि ब्रह्मसंसिद्ध्यै ततो मेऽसौ भविष्यति .. 67 ..
ततःप्रभृति चित्ते स्वे धारयामि सदैव तु ..
विश्वरूपं तथा सूर्यं हृत्पंकजनिवासिनम् .. 68 ..
ततो दिक्षु दिगन्तेषु गगने धरणीतले ..
तमेकं चैव पश्यामि नान्यत्किंचिद्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 69 ..
अहं च तेजसा युक्तस्तत्प्रभावेण संस्थितः .. 6.185.70 ..
एवं मे स गुरुर्जातः शरकारो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
शृणुध्वं कन्यका जाता गुरुत्वे मे यथा पुरा .. 71 ..
सर्वसंगपरित्यागी यदाहं निर्गतो गृहात् ..
ममानुपृष्ठतश्चैव ततो भार्या विनिर्गता .. 72 ..
शिशुं पुत्रं समादाय कन्यामेकां च शोभनाम्..
ततोऽहं भार्यया प्रोक्तो वानप्रस्थाश्रमे स्थितः..73..
5.184.m:
‘Yoga, which gives rise to knowledge of Brahman, comes from single-mindedness; / it will not be mine otherwise. Therefore, I shall perform restraint of the mind / for the complete realization of Brahman; from that, it will come to be.’ 67
From then on, in my own mind, I always hold / the universal-formed sun residing in the lotus of the heart. 68
Then, in the quarters, in the ends of the quarters, in the sky, and on the surface of the earth, / I see only that One, and nothing else, O best of brahmins. 69
And I, endowed with splendor, remain by its power. 70
Thus that arrow-maker became my guru, O best of brahmins; / hear how formerly a young girl became my guru. 71
When, renouncing all attachment, I departed from home, / my wife followed right behind me. 72
Taking a young son and a beautiful girl, / I, having entered the forest-dweller stage, was then addressed by my wife: 73

5.184.s:
kuru me vacanaṃ muktiratraiva hi bhaviṣyati..
brahmacārī gṛhastho vā vānaprastho'thavā yatiḥ..
yadi syātsaṃyatātmā sa nūnaṃ muktimavāpnuyāt..74..
athavā māṃ parityajya yadi yāsyasi cānyataḥ..
tadahaṃ ca mariṣyāmi satyametadasaṃśayam..75..
mṛtāyāṃ mayi te bālāvetāvanumariṣyataḥ..
kumārī ca kumāraśca tasmānnātha dayāṃ kuru..76..
mā vrajasva paraṃ tīrthaṃ parijānannapi svayam..
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetrametatpuṇyataraṃ smṛtam..77..
sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ śrutametanmayā vibho..
vadatāṃ brāhmaṇendrāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ tapasvinām..78..
śloko'yaṃ bahudhā nātha kīrtyamāno mayā vibho..
viśvāmitrasya vaktreṇa sanmuneḥ satyavādinaḥ..79..
punaṃti sarvatīrthāni snānadānādasaṃśayam..
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ smaraṇādapi pāvayet..6.185.8...
5.184.d:
कुरु मे वचनं मुक्तिरत्रैव हि भविष्यति..
ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थो वा वानप्रस्थोऽथवा यतिः..
यदि स्यात्संयतात्मा स नूनं मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात्..74..
अथवा मां परित्यज्य यदि यास्यसि चान्यतः..
तदहं च मरिष्यामि सत्यमेतदसंशयम्..75..
मृतायां मयि ते बालावेतावनुमरिष्यतः..
कुमारी च कुमारश्च तस्मान्नाथ दयां कुरु..76..
मा व्रजस्व परं तीर्थं परिजानन्नपि स्वयम्..
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रमेतत्पुण्यतरं स्मृतम्..77..
सर्वेषामेव तीर्थानां श्रुतमेतन्मया विभो..
वदतां ब्राह्मणेन्द्राणां तथान्येषां तपस्विनाम्..78..
श्लोकोऽयं बहुधा नाथ कीर्त्यमानो मया विभो..
विश्वामित्रस्य वक्त्रेण सन्मुनेः सत्यवादिनः..79..
पुनंति सर्वतीर्थानि स्नानदानादसंशयम्..
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं स्मरणादपि पावयेत्..6.185.8...
5.184.m:
‘Heed my words: liberation will certainly happen right here! / Whether a student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or an ascetic, / if he has a self-controlled mind, he surely attains liberation. 74
Otherwise, if you abandon me and go elsewhere, / then I shall die; this is true without doubt.’ 75
When I am dead, these two children will follow me in death, / both the girl and the boy; therefore, my lord, have compassion.
Do not go to any other sacred ford, though you know it yourself; / this sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara is known to be far more holy.
I have heard this said of all the sacred fords, O powerful lord, / by the foremost of brahmins as well as by other ascetics.
This verse has been repeated many times, O lord, as heard by me, / from the mouth of Viśvāmitra, that virtuous, truth-speaking sage:
All sacred fords cleanse without doubt through bath and gift; / but the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara purifies even by remembrance.’

5.184.s:
tataḥ kṛcchrātpratijñātaṃ mayāśramaniṣevaṇam..
vānaprasthodbhavaṃ vā syāttato'haṃ tatra saṃsthitaḥ..81..
tatrasthasya hi me kanyā krīḍate parataḥ sthitā..
valayāpūritābhyāṃ ca prakoṣṭhābhyāṃ tatastataḥ .. 82 ..
yathāyathā sā kurute kandamūlaphalāśanam ..
tanutvaṃ yāti kāyena tathā caiva dinedine .. 83 ..
tato me jāyate duḥkhaṃ teṣāṃ patana saṃbhavam ..
kasyacittvatha kālasya saṃjātaṃ valayatrayam ..
tasyā haste tatastābhyāṃ śabdaḥ saṃjāyate mithaḥ .. 84 ..
tataḥ kālena mahatā tābhyāmekaṃ vyavasthitam ..
na saṃgharṣo na śabdaśca tatrasthasya ca jāyate .. 85 ..
tadvicintya mayā so'pi hyāśramaḥ parivarjitaḥ ..
cintitaṃ ca mayā citte kṛtvā caivaṃ suniścayam .. 86 ..

5.184.m:
Then with difficulty I undertook to dwell in a hermitage, / entering upon the forest-dweller's stage; and so I stayed there.
While I was staying there, the girl was playing nearby, / her forearms on both sides filled with bangles here and there.
As she ate [nothing but] edible tubers, roots, and fruits, / her body grew thinner and thinner day by day.
Then sorrow arose in me, born of their falling off. / But after some time, only three bangles remained / on her arm, and from them a clinking sound was produced together.
Then after a long time, only one of them remained; / and no friction and no sound arose from it as it rested there.
Pondering that, I abandoned even that hermitage; / and in my heart I reflected, having formed this firm resolve:
‘With many there is perpetual quarrel; with two there is friction. / I will wander alone, just like the girl’s bangle.’

5.184.m:
Then, having abandoned my sleeping wife with the child, / I traveled far along the path, where she would not find me.
Sleeping wherever the sun set, eating whatever was obtained, / I wandered the surface of the earth, abandoning the bond of worldly existence.
Then, O brahmins, knowledge arose in me thus by degrees, / especially of the past, the future, and the present.
In this way, O best of the twice-born, that little girl became my teacher.
All this has been related to you because I was questioned about my guru; / I am not speaking untruth before you in any way.
In these six ways knowledge was born in me; / through these arose transcendental knowledge that produces conviction in you.
Sūta said: / Then all those brahmins, the best of the twice-born, questioned him: / ‘Having abandoned the forest-dweller’s hermitage, your wife, and your child, / where did you go then? Tell us, and how long did you remain there?’

5.184.m:
The guest said: / Afraid, I [passed through] thousands and hundreds of villages, / sleeping wherever the sun set, O best of the twice-born, / through innumerable hundreds of years.
The foremost sacred fords were seen, and likewise sacred shrines; / lofty mountains were seen, and rivers of pure water.
While residing in Vārāṇasī, it was known by me on my own / that a sacrifice by Pitāmaha [Brahmā] was to take place in this place of mine.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, I arrived quickly out of curiosity: / ‘What kind of sacrifice will that be, where Pitāmaha is the sacrificer?’
Sūta said: / In the meantime, all the gods, accompanied by Indra, arrived, / placing Vāsudeva and Maheśvara at their head.
Having reached the proper turn, the officiating priests such as Pulastya, / and Brahmā himself, clad in a deer skin, also arrived.
Then they were pleased with that knowledge of his; / and all the gods, being granters of boons, said to him:

5.184.m:
‘Therefore choose a boon—hail to you!—ask for whatever you desire. / We will surely give it to you, even if it is very difficult to obtain.’
The guest said: / ‘If the gods are pleased and grant me a boon, / I ask for godhood in this very body,
together with a sacrificial share equal to that of the other gods, / and especially, O best of gods, a dwelling situated above.’
The gods said: / ‘You will certainly become a god and dwell in heaven / in this very body, but devoid of a sacrificial share.
If we were to give a sacrificial share to you, a human, O brahmin, / the Vedic revelation would become unauthoritative by our giving it to you.’
The guest said: / ‘I have no need of godhood if it is devoid of a sacrificial share. / Therefore, I shall strive in such a way that liberation may occur.’
Hearing that, [Brahmā], born of the lotus, with folded hands, said to all the gods: / ‘Let all the deities listen to the beneficial words I speak.

5.184.m:
This brahmin has come from far away to my sacrifice; / being a Nāgara in particular, he is a vessel born of wisdom.
Moreover, since a boon was promised to him by all the gods, / let what is desired be given to him, O best of gods.’
Maheśvara said: / ‘Let the best of gods listen to how I will explain / in what way his satisfaction may always be greater than a sacrificial share.
Hari is remembered as the lord of this sacrifice that is being performed; / for this reason that god is called the Person of Sacrifice.
From this day onward, whatever ancestral rite takes place among mortals, / whether offered to gods or to ancestors, he shall be placed at the conclusion of it.
Having recited his name, and then reciting that of the Person of Sacrifice, / food is to be given to the brahmin, O best of the twice-born.
Thereby his satisfaction will always be greater than at the conclusion of a sacrifice. / Whatever ancestral rite may be performed without giving to him,

5.184.m:
all of that will become fruitless, like an oblation poured onto ashes. / And whoever will worship him at the conclusion of the rite to the All-gods—
Equaling the name of Viṣṇu, it shall become imperishable, / even if very little is given, provided it is given with a mind purified by faith. // 117
And whoever does not worship him at a śrāddha or a vaiśvadeva sacrifice, / everything he has performed will turn out to be futile. // 118
When he is pleased, all the gods will attain delight; / and the ancestors come to him [who gives], turning away when he turns away, and facing him when he faces [the guest]. // 119
Hearing those words of Maheśvara at that time, all the gods, / headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, joyfully replied, “So be it!” // 6.185.120
From that time forth, the worship of the guest was established. / Therefore, with all effort, worship of the guest must always be performed / at the sacrifice of the Supreme Person, and never for oneself alone. // 121
The Guest said: / “Here is my sacred ford where I performed austerity / in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara in ancient times, O best of twice-borns. // 122

5.184.s:
aṃgārakeṇa saṃyuktā caturthī syādyadā tithiḥ ..
sāṃnidhyaṃ tatra kāryaṃ ca sarvairdevaiśca taddine .. 123 ..
kuryāttatraiva yaḥ snānaṃ tasminnahani saṃsthite ..
sarvatīrthaphalaṃ tasya jāyatāṃ vaḥ prasādataḥ .. 124 ..
tathāstviti tataḥ sarve'tithiṃ procuḥ surottamāḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare prāha pulastyarṣiḥ pitāmaham ..125.. ..
pulastya uvāca .. ..
ṛtvijaḥ sakalā devāḥ saṃsthitāḥ kautukānvitāḥ ..
uttiṣṭhaṃtu ca te śīghraṃ yajñakarmaprasiddhaye .. 126 ..
etasminnaṃtare sarve tasya vākyapraṇoditāḥ ..
utthitā ṛtvijo ye ca svāni sthānāni bhejire ..
tataḥ pravavṛte yajñaḥ sapunardvijasattamāḥ ..
kurvatā yajñakarmāṇi homapūrvāṇi yāni ca .. 127 ..
5.184.d:
अंगारकेण संयुक्ता चतुर्थी स्याद्यदा तिथिः ..
सांनिध्यं तत्र कार्यं च सर्वैर्देवैश्च तद्दिने .. 123 ..
कुर्यात्तत्रैव यः स्नानं तस्मिन्नहनि संस्थिते ..
सर्वतीर्थफलं तस्य जायतां वः प्रसादतः .. 124 ..
तथास्त्विति ततः सर्वेऽतिथिं प्रोचुः सुरोत्तमाः ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राह पुलस्त्यर्षिः पितामहम् ..125.. ..
पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
ऋत्विजः सकला देवाः संस्थिताः कौतुकान्विताः ..
उत्तिष्ठंतु च ते शीघ्रं यज्ञकर्मप्रसिद्धये .. 126 ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सर्वे तस्य वाक्यप्रणोदिताः ..
उत्थिता ऋत्विजो ये च स्वानि स्थानानि भेजिरे ..
ततः प्रववृते यज्ञः सपुनर्द्विजसत्तमाः ..
कुर्वता यज्ञकर्माणि होमपूर्वाणि यानि च .. 127 ..
5.184.m:
Whenever the fourth lunar day falls together with Tuesday, / presence must be established there on that day by all the gods. // 123
Whoever performs ritual ablution right there, that day being present, / let him obtain the fruit of all sacred fords by your grace!” // 124
Then all the best of gods said to the Guest, “So be it!” / In the meantime, the seer Pulastya spoke to the Grandfather: // 125
Pulastya said: / “All the priests, the gods, are standing eager with curiosity. / Let them rise quickly for the successful performance of the sacrificial rites.” // 126
In the meantime, impelled by his words, all the officiating priests / arose and took their respective places. / Then, O best of twice-borns, that sacrifice proceeded once again, / as they performed the sacrificial rites beginning with the oblations. // 127

5.184.s:
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye tīrthotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nā
ma pañcāśītyuttaraśata tamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 185 .. .. cha ..
5.184.d:
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये तीर्थोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं ना
म पञ्चाशीत्युत्तरशत तमोऽध्यायः .. 185 .. .. छ ..
5.184.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Origin and Greatness of the Sacred Ford', in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse compilation in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa. // 185

5.185.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
bhūya eva mahābhāga vada māhātmyamuttamam ..
atitheḥ kṛtyamasmākaṃ vistareṇa ca sūtaja .. 1 ..
5.185.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
भूय एव महाभाग वद माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ..
अतिथेः कृत्यमस्माकं विस्तरेण च सूतज .. 1 ..
5.185.m: The seers said: / “O highly fortunate one, son of Sūta, declare once more in full detail / the supreme māhātmya of the guest and our duty [toward him].” // 1

5.185.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śṛṇvantu munayaḥ sarve māhātmyamidamuttamam ..
yena saṃśrutamātreṇa naśyetpāpaṃ dinodbhavam .. 2 ..
5.185.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
शृण्वन्तु मुनयः सर्वे माहात्म्यमिदमुत्तमम् ..
येन संश्रुतमात्रेण नश्येत्पापं दिनोद्भवम् .. 2 ..
5.185.m: Sūta said: / “Let all the sages listen to this supreme māhātmya, / by merely hearing which the sin born of the day is destroyed, // 2

5.185.s: yanmayā ca śrutaṃ pūrvaṃ sakāśātsvapituḥ śubham .. 3 ..
5.185.d: यन्मया च श्रुतं पूर्वं सकाशात्स्वपितुः शुभम् .. 3 ..
5.185.m: which was previously heard by me as auspicious from my father's presence. // 3

5.185.s:
gṛhasthānāṃ paro dharmo nānyo'styatithipūjanāt ..
atitherna ca doṣosti tasyātikramaṇena ca .. 4 ..
5.185.d:
गृहस्थानां परो धर्मो नान्योऽस्त्यतिथिपूजनात् ..
अतिथेर्न च दोषोस्ति तस्यातिक्रमणेन च .. 4 ..
5.185.m: For householders there is no higher duty than the worship of a guest; / there is no fault in a guest, nor in passing beyond him. // 4

5.185.s:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate ..
sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyamādāya gacchati .. 5 ..
5.185.d:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते ..
स दत्त्वा दुष्कृतं तस्मै पुण्यमादाय गच्छति .. 5 ..
5.185.m: From whose house a guest turns away with his hopes shattered, / he goes away leaving his misdeeds to that host and taking away his merit. // 5

5.185.s:
satyaṃ śaucaṃ tapo'dhītaṃ dattamiṣṭaṃ śataṃ samāḥ ..
tasya sarvamidaṃ naṣṭamatithiṃ yo na pūjayet .. 6 ..
5.185.d:
सत्यं शौचं तपोऽधीतं दत्तमिष्टं शतं समाः ..
तस्य सर्वमिदं नष्टमतिथिं यो न पूजयेत् .. 6 ..
5.185.m: Truth, purification, austerity, study, sacrifices, and gifts made for a hundred years— / all this is lost for him who does not worship a guest. // 6

5.185.s:
dūrādatithayo yasya gṛhamāyāṃti nirvṛtāḥ ..
sa gṛhastha iti proktaḥ śeṣāśca gṛharakṣiṇaḥ .. 7 ..
5.185.d:
दूरादतिथयो यस्य गृहमायांति निर्वृताः ..
स गृहस्थ इति प्रोक्तः शेषाश्च गृहरक्षिणः .. 7 ..
5.185.m: He to whose house guests come contented from afar / is called a true householder; the others are merely guardians of a house. // 7

5.185.s:
na purākṛtapuṇyānāṃ narāṇāmiha bhūtale ..
trīnetānpratihanyaṃte śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ śubhā giraḥ .. 8 ..
5.185.d:
न पुराकृतपुण्यानां नराणामिह भूतले ..
त्रीनेतान्प्रतिहन्यंते श्राद्धं दानं शुभा गिरः .. 8 ..
5.185.m: For men on this earth who have performed no prior merit, / these three are obstructed: ancestral offerings, gifts, and kind words. // 8

5.185.s:
tuṣṭe'tithau gṛhasthasya tuṣṭāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ ..
vimukhe vimukhāḥ sarvā bhavaṃti ca na saṃśayaḥ 9 ..
5.185.d:
तुष्टेऽतिथौ गृहस्थस्य तुष्टाः स्युः सर्वदेवताः ..
विमुखे विमुखाः सर्वा भवंति च न संशयः 9 ..
5.185.m: When a guest is pleased, all deities become pleased with the householder; / when he turns away, all turn away, without a doubt. // 9

5.185.s:
tasmāttoṣayitavyaśca gṛhasthena sadā'tithiḥ ..
apyātmanaḥ pradānena yadīcchetpuṇyamātmanaḥ .. .. 6.186.10 ..
5.185.d:
तस्मात्तोषयितव्यश्च गृहस्थेन सदाऽतिथिः ..
अप्यात्मनः प्रदानेन यदीच्छेत्पुण्यमात्मनः .. .. 6.186.10 ..
5.185.m: Therefore, a guest must always be gratified by a householder, / even by offering himself, if he desires merit for himself. // 6.186.10

5.185.s:
trividhastvatithiḥ prokto gṛhasthānāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
tasyāhaṃ vacmi vaḥ kālaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ .. 11 ..
5.185.d:
त्रिविधस्त्वतिथिः प्रोक्तो गृहस्थानां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तस्याहं वच्मि वः कालं शृणुध्वं सुसमाहिताः .. 11 ..
5.185.m: A guest is declared to be threefold for householders, O best of twice-borns. / I shall tell you their proper time; listen attentively: // 11

5.185.s:
śrāddhīyo vaiśvadevīyaḥ sūryoḍhaśca tṛtīyakaḥ ..
ye cānye bhojanārthīyāste sāmānyāḥ prakīrtitā .. 12 ..
5.185.d:
श्राद्धीयो वैश्वदेवीयः सूर्योढश्च तृतीयकः ..
ये चान्ये भोजनार्थीयास्ते सामान्याः प्रकीर्तिता .. 12 ..
5.185.m: one belonging to the śrāddha, one belonging to the vaiśvadeva, and the third is the one brought by the sun [at evening]; / those others who come seeking food are designated as ordinary ones. // 12

5.185.s:
sāṃkalpe vihite śrāddhe pitṝṇāṃ bhojanodbhave ..
samāgacchati yaḥ kāle tasmiñchrāddhīya eva saḥ .. 13 ..
5.185.d:
सांकल्पे विहिते श्राद्धे पितॄणां भोजनोद्भवे ..
समागच्छति यः काले तस्मिञ्छ्राद्धीय एव सः .. 13 ..
5.185.m: When a deliberate śrāddha has been arranged for the dining of the ancestors, / he who arrives at that time is indeed a guest of the śrāddha. // 13

5.185.s:
dūrādhvānaṃ pathi śrāṃtaṃ vaiśvadevāṃta āgatam ..
atithiṃ taṃ vijānīyānnātithiḥ pūrvamāgataḥ .. 14 ..
5.185.d:
दूराध्वानं पथि श्रांतं वैश्वदेवांत आगतम् ..
अतिथिं तं विजानीयान्नातिथिः पूर्वमागतः .. 14 ..
5.185.m: One who comes at the end of the vaiśvadeva, weary from travel on a long road, / one should know him as a guest; one who arrived earlier is not a guest. // 14

5.185.s:
priyo vā yadi vā dveṣyo mūrkhaḥ paṃḍita eva vā ..
vaiśvadeve tu saṃprāptaḥ so'tithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ .. 15 ..
5.185.d:
प्रियो वा यदि वा द्वेष्यो मूर्खः पंडित एव वा ..
वैश्वदेवे तु संप्राप्तः सोऽतिथिः स्वर्गसंक्रमः .. 15 ..
5.185.m: Whether dear or disliked, a fool or indeed a scholar, / if he arrives at the vaiśvadeva sacrifice, that guest is a bridge to heaven. // 15

5.185.s:
na pṛcchedgotracaraṇaṃ na sthānaṃ vedameva ca ..
dṛṣṭvā yajñopavītaṃ ca bhojayettaṃ prabhaktitaḥ .. 16 ..
5.185.d:
न पृच्छेद्गोत्रचरणं न स्थानं वेदमेव च ..
दृष्ट्वा यज्ञोपवीतं च भोजयेत्तं प्रभक्तितः .. 16 ..
5.185.m: One should not ask his lineage, conduct, dwelling, or Veda; / seeing his sacred thread, one should feed him with great devotion. // 16

5.185.s:
śrāddhe vā vaiśvadeve vā yadyāgacchati nātithiḥ ..
ghṛtāhutiṃ tato dadyāttannāmnā ca havirbhuji .. 17 ..
5.185.d:
श्राद्धे वा वैश्वदेवे वा यद्यागच्छति नातिथिः ..
घृताहुतिं ततो दद्यात्तन्नाम्ना च हविर्भुजि .. 17 ..
5.185.m: If no guest arrives at the śrāddha or at the vaiśvadeva, / one should then offer an oblation of clarified butter into the fire in his name. // 17

5.185.s:
aśaktyā bhojyadānasya deyaṃ bhaktyā tataḥ param ..
tasyānnamapi tu stokaṃ yena tuṣṭiṃ pragacchati .. 18 ..
5.185.d:
अशक्त्या भोज्यदानस्य देयं भक्त्या ततः परम् ..
तस्यान्नमपि तु स्तोकं येन तुष्टिं प्रगच्छति .. 18 ..
5.185.m: If unable to provide a full meal, something further should be given with devotion— / even a little of his food, whereby he becomes satisfied. // 18

5.185.s:
tathānyaśca tṛtīyastu sūryoḍho'tithirucyate ..
kṛte tu bhojane yastu rātrau vā cādhigacchati..
tasya śaktyā pradātavyaṃ sasyaṃ ca gṛhamedhinā..19..
sūryoḍho yasya saṃprāpto gṛhātpūjāṃ vinā vrajet..
nirāśaḥ pātakaṃ tasya nijaṃ dattvā prayāti saḥ..6.186.2...
5.185.d:
तथान्यश्च तृतीयस्तु सूर्योढोऽतिथिरुच्यते ..
कृते तु भोजने यस्तु रात्रौ वा चाधिगच्छति..
तस्य शक्त्या प्रदातव्यं सस्यं च गृहमेधिना..19..
सूर्योढो यस्य संप्राप्तो गृहात्पूजां विना व्रजेत्..
निराशः पातकं तस्य निजं दत्त्वा प्रयाति सः..6.186.2...
5.185.m:
And the third guest is called the one brought by the sun; / he who arrives after the meal has been taken, or at night, / should be given grain by the householder according to his capacity. // 19
He who has arrived brought by the sun, if he departs from a house without worship, / leaves behind his own sin disappointed, and departs. // 6.186.20

5.185.s:
tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṃ vākcaturthī ca sūnṛtā..
etānyapi satāṃ gehe nocchidyaṃte kadācana..21..
5.185.d:
तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक्चतुर्थी च सूनृता..
एतान्यपि सतां गेहे नोच्छिद्यंते कदाचन..21..
5.185.m: Grass [for a seat], earth [for rest], water, and fourthly pleasant speech— / these are never lacking in the houses of the virtuous. // 21

5.185.s:
svāgatenāgnayastṛptiṃ gṛhasthasya prayāṃti ca ..
āsanena vrajettuṣṭiṃ svayaṃbhūḥ prapitāmahaḥ .. 22..
5.185.d:
स्वागतेनाग्नयस्तृप्तिं गृहस्थस्य प्रयांति च ..
आसनेन व्रजेत्तुष्टिं स्वयंभूः प्रपितामहः .. 22..
5.185.m: By a welcome the fires of the householder attain satisfaction; / by a seat the self-manifest Great-Grandfather attains contentment; // 22

5.185.s:
argheṇa śaṃbhuḥ pādyena sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
bhojyadānena viṣṇuḥ syātsarvadevamayo'tithiḥ .. 23 ..
5.185.d:
अर्घेण शंभुः पाद्येन सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
भोज्यदानेन विष्णुः स्यात्सर्वदेवमयोऽतिथिः .. 23 ..
5.185.m: by the respectful offering Śambhu is pleased; by water for the feet all gods with Indra; / by the gift of food Viṣṇu is pleased, for the guest embodies all deities. // 23

5.185.s:
tasmātpūjyaḥ sadā viprā bhojanīyo viśeṣataḥ ..
nāmāpyuccārya bhojyo'nyo brāhmaṇo gṛhamedhinā .. 24 ..
5.185.d:
तस्मात्पूज्यः सदा विप्रा भोजनीयो विशेषतः ..
नामाप्युच्चार्य भोज्योऽन्यो ब्राह्मणो गृहमेधिना .. 24 ..
5.185.m: Therefore, O brahmins, he must always be worshiped and fed especially; / any other brahmin should also be fed by the householder after uttering his name. // 24

5.185.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭa keśvarakṣetramāhātmye'tithimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaḍaśītyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 186 .. ..
5.185.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाट केश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽतिथिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम षडशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 186 .. ..
5.185.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Guest', in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of the Glorious Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse compilation in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa. // 186
